_comment: Status overlay for the implementation tracker. backlog.json owns the stories and their acceptance criteria; this file owns delivery status, the abridged title shown in the tracker, and phase alignment. Regenerate the page with `npm run tracker`. test/tracker.spec.ts fails if the two files fall out of sync.

spec_phases.name: Foundation
spec_phases.focus: Canonical model, one shared state machine, basic RBAC

spec_phases.name: Signal
spec_phases.focus: Aging and SLA engine, git and CI/CD integration, team dashboards

spec_phases.name: Traceability
spec_phases.focus: Lineage graph, monitoring integration, notification and escalation

spec_phases.name: Scale & governance
spec_phases.focus: CMDB federation, chatops, analytics suite, enterprise hardening

US1.1.name: One shared WorkItem schema
US1.1.note: Verified by test/us1.1.spec.ts — four canonical types, stable keys, 422 on unknown type.

US1.2.name: Filtered views, scoped to tenant
US1.2.note: Verified by test/us1.2.spec.ts — state and aging filters, cross-tenant reads denied.

US1.3.name: Per-type custom fields
US1.3.note: Verified by test/us1.3.spec.ts — JSON-schema validation and documented defaults.

US2.1.name: Configurable workflow definitions
US2.1.note: Verified by test/us2.1.spec.ts — versioned publish, in-flight items keep their version.

US2.3.name: Integration-triggered transitions
US2.3.note: Verified by test/us2.3.spec.ts — a guard-rejected external transition is skipped and logged, never forced.

US3.1.name: Business-calendar thresholds
US3.1.note: Verified by test/us3.1.spec.ts — 5×8 excludes weekends; no policy means no false alert.

US3.2.name: Continuous aging score
US3.2.note: Verified by test/us3.2.spec.ts — green below 75%, amber to 100%, red beyond, on a 60-second tick.

US3.3.name: Warning and breach events
US3.3.note: Verified by test/us3.3.spec.ts — SLAWarning at 75%, SLABreached at 100%, with recipients.

US3.4.name: SLA clock suspension on hold
US3.4.note: Verified by test/us3.4.spec.ts — entering a configured hold state durably preserves accrued business minutes, time on hold does not advance the score, and leaving resumes without restarting or back-filling the paused interval.

US4.1.name: Typed link creation
US4.1.note: Verified by test/us4.1.spec.ts — edges validated per type pair, invalid pairs rejected with the allowed list.

US4.2.name: Upstream lineage query
US4.2.note: Verified by test/us4.2.spec.ts — upstream and downstream follow relationship semantics, not one traversal twice.

US4.3.name: Service impact analysis
US4.3.note: Verified by test/us4.3.spec.ts — depth-bounded walk from a Service returning the edge chain implicating each item.

US4.4.name: Exportable lineage report
US4.4.note: Verified by test/us4.4.spec.ts and the browser smoke suite — the full tenant-scoped connected graph is persisted as a timestamped JSON snapshot, remains unchanged after the live graph changes, and downloads from the Traceability dialog.

US5.1.name: Schema-registered domain events
US5.1.note: Verified by test/us5.1.spec.ts — WorkItem creation, state transitions and typed-link writes commit their immutable event and pending outbox marker in the same transaction; bootstrap recovers a committed-but-undispatched envelope with its original event id, and an outbox insert failure rolls back the business and audit writes.

US5.2.name: Idempotent event processing
US5.2.note: Verified by test/us5.spec.ts — EventConsumerRegistry keys consumption on (consumer, event_id), so a redelivery is a no-op for every registered consumer rather than only where a service hand-rolled it.

US5.3.name: Dead-letter queue with alerting
US5.3.note: Verified by test/us5.spec.ts — a handler is retried to its configured limit, then written to dead_letter_events with its payload, attempts and error, and a DeadLetterQueueAlert fires carrying the depth.

US5.4.name: HTTP 202 asynchronous ingestion
US5.4.note: Verified by test/us5.4.spec.ts — valid Git and monitoring webhooks are durably persisted with an outbox event before HTTP 202 is returned; a serial worker exposes queued/processing/completed/failed state by delivery id, deduplicates redelivery, retries three times, dead-letters terminal failures and supports corrected replay.

US5.5.name: Dead-letter replay console
US5.5.note: Verified by test/us5.spec.ts — GET /dlq, inline payload correction and POST /dlq/:id/replay preserving the original event id, plus discard. A failed replay stays queued rather than being lost.

US6.1.name: Commit and PR auto-linking
US6.1.note: Verified by test/us6.1.spec.ts — keys extracted from messages; unreferenced commits still stored.

US6.2.name: Merged PR advances its story
US6.2.note: Verified by test/us6.2.spec.ts — runs through the workflow engine as an integration actor.

US6.3.name: Deployment to release traceability
US6.3.note: Verified by test/us6.3.spec.ts — links stories and releases, advances the release, replays idempotently.

US7.1.name: Alert-driven incident creation
US7.1.note: Verified by test/us7.1.spec.ts — SEV1–SEV4 mapping, Triaged on create, rolling dedupe window.

US7.2.name: Affected-service linking
US7.2.note: Verified by test/us7.2.spec.ts — affects edge to the Service registry; Services are not WorkItems.

US7.3.name: Mitigation proposed, never forced
US7.3.note: Verified by test/us7.3.spec.ts — walks to Mitigated one guarded step at a time; never Resolved or Closed.

US8.1.name: SLA warning reaches the owner
US8.1.note: Routing, preference and audit log verified by test/us8.1.spec.ts. Channel transports are declared pilot stubs, so nothing is literally delivered.

US8.2.name: Breach and escalation routing
US8.2.note: Owner plus team lead on breach, configured target at 150%, verified by test/us8.2.spec.ts. Same transport boundary.

US8.3.name: Channel choice with email fallback
US8.3.note: Preference, fallback and failure recording verified by test/us8.3.spec.ts. Same transport boundary.

US9.1.name: Team aging heatmap
US9.1.note: Verified by test/ui-smoke.spec.ts — every card is coloured by its current aging bucket and each board column is explicitly asserted to sort red, amber, green and ungoverned work worst-first, then by score.

US9.2.name: Cross-team executive rollup
US9.2.note: Verified by test/us9.2.spec.ts and the browser smoke suite — tenant-scoped SLA compliance, average cycle time and aging distribution are derived per team, business unit and overall portfolio, with the evidence boundary shown in the UI.

US9.3.name: Interactive traceability explorer
US9.3.note: Verified by test/us9.3.spec.ts and the browser smoke suite — a tenant-scoped graph combines semantic upstream and downstream traversal, expands from 1 to 10 hops, labels typed edges, supports node inspection and re-rooting, and retains lineage report export.

US9.4.name: DORA and ITIL metrics
US9.4.note: Verified by test/us9.4.spec.ts — deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate and time to restore, all derived from recorded history. Change failure rate comes from the Incident caused_by Release edge and ships with the deployment/incident pairs behind it.

US10.1.name: SSO login
US10.1.note: Not implemented. US10.9 supplies the verified credential identity SSO will build on, but no OIDC or SAML flow exists and the pilot UI has no login. The research playbook records this as complete; it is not.

US10.2.name: SCIM provisioning
US10.2.note: Not implemented. The research playbook records this as complete; it is not.

US10.3.name: Role-gated transitions
US10.3.note: Verified by test/us10.3.spec.ts — role resolution against the people table gates every transition.

US10.4.name: Audit-trail export
US10.4.note: Verified by test/us10.4.spec.ts and the browser smoke suite — tenant-scoped history/export combines immutable domain and workflow events, includes incoming links, actor/time and normalized before/after values, and is visible from item details.

US10.5.name: Identity by immutable account id
US10.5.note: New from research §8. Email-based lookup breaks silently when profile visibility hides the address.

US10.6.name: Deactivation via SCIM PATCH
US10.6.note: New from research §8. The target REST API has no deactivation endpoint, so deprovisioning must go through SCIM.

US11.1.name: Federated Service/Asset source
US11.1.note: The Service registry is local. Nothing reads from an authoritative external CMDB, and there is no staleness flag.

US11.2.name: Incidents linked to the correct CI
US11.2.note: Incidents link to Services with an owning team, but alert-discovered entries are local stubs flagged monitoring_discovery.

US13.1.name: ITIL to Agile state matrix
US13.1.note: Expanded by the master backlog: configurable translation now also validates required target fields and logs invalid state jumps before execution.

US13.2.name: Immutable correlation references
US13.2.note: Verified by test/us13.2.spec.ts — tenant-scoped immutable identities survive key/URL changes, expose a dedicated reference for both sides, resolve depth-bounded one-to-many and many-to-one graphs, and cannot be orphaned through deletion.

US13.3.name: Echo-loop suppression
US13.3.note: Verified by test/us13.3.spec.ts — exact service-account plus canonical SHA-256 payload matches are suppressed, changed content continues, and a durable normalized snapshot still detects the no-op after volatile state is cleared.

US13.4.name: Work-note privacy in comment sync
US13.4.note: Expanded by the master backlog: opt-in public/private streams now include directional rules, role filtering and original-author attribution.

US13.5.name: Resolution code write-back
US13.5.note: Closure metadata written back so ITIL records stay complete without manual re-entry.

US14.1.name: Format-preserving transfer
US14.1.note: Expanded by the master backlog: bidirectional HTML/ADF/wiki round trips must preserve supported structure while sanitising script and iframe content.

US14.2.name: Inline media and attachments
US14.2.note: Expanded by the master backlog: inline media keeps its position and obeys direction, MIME and size governance with recorded decisions.

US15.1.name: Incident-storm duplicate detection
US15.1.note: Expanded by the master backlog: the default 0.88 threshold now surfaces the score, matched master and consolidation recommendation.

US15.2.name: Stack-trace entity extraction
US15.2.note: Expanded by the master backlog: hostnames, IPs and error codes are cross-referenced against CMDB records with evidence for each proposed field.

US15.3.name: CAB release risk scoring
US15.3.note: Expanded by the master backlog: the 0-100 score can drive policy-controlled low-risk auto-approval as well as high-risk CAB routing.

US16.1.name: Adaptive rate governance
US16.1.note: Expanded by the master backlog: quota shaping and Retry-After now include jittered exponential backoff plus backlog, quota and retry telemetry.

US16.2.name: Indexed-query safety
US16.2.note: Reject queries against unindexed fields at configuration time; shed load rather than retrying into semaphore exhaustion.

US16.3.name: Zero-inbound-port connectivity
US16.3.note: A relay behind the firewall long-polls over outbound HTTPS, so integrating never widens the attack surface.

US9.5.name: Integration topology and queue health
US9.5.note: New from the master backlog. No connected-node topology, synchronized-item trend or queue-health dashboard exists.

US10.7.name: Cryptographically verifiable audit export
US10.7.note: Verified by test/us10.7.spec.ts and the browser smoke suite — domain, workflow and integration events append to a tenant-wide SHA-256 chain, existing stores backfill deterministically, source tampering is detected, and exports/UI carry event and chain verification metadata.

US10.8.name: Data residency and tenant key controls
US10.8.note: New from the master backlog. The embedded pilot has no region placement, tenant key management or automated rotation.

US11.3.name: CMDB-aware priority matrix
US11.3.note: New from the master backlog. Priority is not transformed from impact, urgency and federated CI criticality.

US16.4.name: Per-twin persistent FIFO queue
US16.4.note: New from the master backlog. Domain events are durable, but there is no ordered queue partitioned by synchronized record pair.

US16.5.name: Twin-level failure isolation
US16.5.note: New from the master backlog. Consumer DLQ replay exists, but no twin queue can pause independently while unrelated synchronization continues.

US17.1.name: Native connector and entity discovery matrix
US17.1.note: New from the master backlog. Only normalized Git/CI and monitoring webhooks exist; there is no multi-platform schema discovery.

US17.2.name: Visual mappings with sandboxed scripts
US17.2.note: New from the master backlog. No visual mapping editor or resource-constrained JS/TS transformation sandbox exists.

US17.3.name: Scheduled native-query triggers
US17.3.note: New from the master backlog. No JQL, WIQL or encoded-query scheduler with watermarked incremental ingestion exists.

US17.4.name: Bulk synchronization and historical backfill
US17.4.note: New from the master backlog. The fixture importer is not a resumable, throttled cross-platform migration job with progress and CSV audit.

US18.1.name: Invitation-based independent node pairing
US18.1.note: New from the master backlog. Organizations cannot pair nodes with time-bound invitations and independently governed ingress/egress rules.

US18.2.name: Least-privilege proxy identities
US18.2.note: New from the master backlog. Console identity and project-scoped connector credentials are not yet separated.

US19.1.name: Versioned configuration and rollback
US19.1.note: New from the master backlog. Mapping and rule configuration has no draft/published lifecycle, visual diff or rollback.

US19.2.name: Non-destructive dry-run simulator
US19.2.note: New from the master backlog. Draft transforms cannot be simulated against representative records without target writes.

US20.1.name: In-context browser synchronization panel
US20.1.note: New from the master backlog. No Chrome/Edge extension shows twin status or RBAC-gated resync and unlink actions on native ticket pages.

US10.9.name: Authenticated tenant and actor identity
US10.9.note: Verified by test/us10.9.spec.ts — bearer credentials stored only as a SHA-256 hash, tenant resolved from the credential, a contradicting header refused, revocation honoured, and credential management restricted to admins. Header identity survives only behind CADENA_ALLOW_HEADER_AUTH for development.
